steps.message:
The C project in /app (the `libqs` library and the `colstat` and `qcalc` programs) does not build, and its makefiles have further defects. Repair the build so that it meets the contract in /app/docs/BUILDING.md: every target there must work from a clean tree with `make -j8`, and `make check`, `make install` and `make DEBUG=1` must behave as documented. Keep the programs' behavior as described in /app/docs/colstat.md and /app/docs/qcalc.md. The repaired project will be built and checked again from a clean copy, including on inputs other than the ones in /app/tests.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

results.content:
Read text file `/app/docs/BUILDING.md`.
1|# Building qs
2|
3|qs is a small C library (`libqs`) with two command-line programs built on it: `colstat`, which
4|prints summary statistics for the columns of a delimited file, and `qcalc`, which evaluates
5|arithmetic expressions. This document is the build contract. Release engineering checks every
6|rule below on a clean checkout before a release is tagged.
7|
8|## 1. Toolchain
9|
10|- GNU make 4.3 and gcc 12 (C11). No other build system is used.
11|- `sh`, `awk`, `sed`, `ar` and `install` from the base system. The build finds them through
12|  `PATH`; it does not use absolute paths for them.
13|- `CC` can be overridden on the command line (`make CC=...`); every compile and link goes
14|  through `$(CC)`.
15|
16|## 2. Source layout
17|
18|| Path | Contents |
19||---|---|
20|| `include/qs/` | Public headers of the library. Hand-written only. |
21|| `lib/<module>/` | Library sources, one directory per module. A module may keep private headers next to its sources. |
22|| `tools/colstat/`, `tools/qcalc/` | The programs. |
23|| `src/ops.def` | The operation table of the expression evaluator (see section 4). |
24|| `VERSION` | The release version, `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` on the first line. |
25|| `build-aux/` | Generator scripts used by the build. |
26|| `tests/unit/` | Unit tests. Every `tests/unit/*.c` file is part of the unit test program; tests register themselves (see `tests/unit/unit.h`). |
27|| `tests/golden/` | Golden cases for the programs (see section 7). |
28|| `man/` | Manual pages, one per program. |
29|| `qs.pc.in` | Template of the pkg-config file. |
30|| `mk/` | Makefile fragments included by the top-level `Makefile`. |
31|
32|The library is every `.c` file under `lib/`; each program is every `.c` file in its directory under
33|`tools/`. Adding a source file to one of those directories adds it to the build without editing
34|the makefiles.
35|
36|## 3. Build output
37|
38|Everything the build writes goes under `build/` and nowhere else:
39|
40|| Path | Contents |
41||---|---|
42|| `build/gen/qs/` | Generated headers. |
43|| `build/obj/` | Object files and dependency files, mirroring the source paths. |
44|| `build/lib/libqs.a` | The static library. |
45|| `build/bin/colstat`, `build/bin/qcalc` | The programs. |
46|| `build/tests/` | Test programs and logs. |
47|
48|`make clean` removes `build/`. A clean tree is the source tree without `build/`.
49|
50|## 4. Generated headers
51|
52|Two headers are generated during the build. Neither is ever kept in the source tree, edited by
53|hand, or committed; a copy outside `build/gen` is a defect, because it can be found before the
54|generated one.
55|
56|| Header | Generated from | By |
57||---|---|---|
58|| `build/gen/qs/version.h` | `VERSION` | `build-aux/mkversion.sh VERSION` (writes to standard output) |
59|| `build/gen/qs/ops.h` | `src/ops.def` | `build-aux/genops.sh src/ops.def` (writes to standard output) |
60|
61|Sources include them as `"qs/version.h"` and `"qs/ops.h"`. `version.h` is public: the umbrella
62|header `qs/qs.h` includes it, and it is installed. `ops.h` is internal to the library and is not
63|installed.
64|
65|`src/ops.def` is the only definition of the operations: their names, symbols, arity, precedence
66|and associativity. The programs must behave as that file says.
67|
68|## 5. Compiler flags
69|
70|There are two configurations. Both treat every warning as an error.
71|
72|| Configuration | How | Flags (in addition to the include paths) |
73||---|---|---|
74|| Release | plain `make` | `-std=c11 -D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L -O2 -DNDEBUG -Wall -Wextra -Werror` |
75|| Debug | `make DEBUG=1` | `-std=c11 -D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L -O0 -g3 -DQS_DEBUG -Wall -Wextra -Werror` |
76|
77|The debug configuration compiles extra tracing code (`QS_DEBUG`) and keeps `assert` active; the
78|release configuration compiles out `assert` (`NDEBUG`). Code must compile cleanly under both.
79|
80|Warnings are fixed in the code. The build must not pass `-w`, any `-Wno-...` option, `-Wno-error`
81|or `-fpermissive`, and sources must not use `#pragma GCC diagnostic` or similar pragmas to
82|silence diagnostics. Fixing a warning must not change what the programs do: `docs/colstat.md`
83|and `docs/qcalc.md` define their behavior, including for inputs the golden cases do not cover.
84|
85|## 6. Targets
86|
87|| Target | Result |
88||---|---|
89|| `all` (first target) | The library and both programs, with the generated headers they need. |
90|| `build/lib/libqs.a`, `build/bin/colstat`, `build/bin/qcalc` | That file and everything it needs. |
91|| `check` | Builds what the tests need, runs the unit tests and the golden cases (section 7). |
92|| `install` | Builds what it installs if needed, then installs (section 8). |
93|| `clean` | Removes `build/`. |
94|
95|Rules every target follows:
96|
97|1. **Clean tree, any parallelism.** Each target above works when it is the first and only target
98|   given on a clean tree, at any `-j` level, every time. A build that only works because make
99|   happened to run jobs in a lucky order is broken. In practice: every file a recipe reads is a
100|   prerequisite of that recipe's target, or is produced before it by a prerequisite; no recipe
101|   relies on the order in which other targets are listed.
102|2. **Linking.** The programs link statically against `build/lib/libqs.a` and against the math
103|   library. Libraries come after the objects that use them on the link line.
104|3. **Incremental builds.** After any change to a source file, a header (hand-written or generated),
105|   `VERSION` or `src/ops.def`, running `make` again rebuilds everything that depends on the change,
106|   so that the programs and the library reflect it. Running `make` twice with nothing changed does
107|   nothing the second time: no compile, archive or link step runs.
108|
109|## 7. Tests
110|
111|`make check` runs two suites and exits with a non-zero status when any test in either suite fails:
112|
113|- The unit test program, built from every `tests/unit/*.c` file and `build/lib/libqs.a`. It exits
114|  non-zero when a check fails.
115|- The golden cases: `sh tests/golden.sh build/bin` runs each case in `tests/golden` and exits
116|  non-zero when a case fails. The case format is described at the top of `tests/golden.sh`.
117|
118|`make check` on a clean tree builds everything both suites need first.
119|
120|## 8. Installation
121|
122|`make install` honors two variables:
123|
124|- `PREFIX`, the installation prefix, `/usr/local` when not given.
125|- `DESTDIR`, prepended to every installed path (for staging and packaging), empty when not given.
126|
127|The installed tree under `$(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)` is exactly:
128|
129|| Path | Mode | Contents |
130||---|---|---|
131|| `bin/colstat`, `bin/qcalc` | 0755 | The programs. |
132|| `lib/libqs.a` | 0644 | The static library. |
133|| `include/qs/*.h` | 0644 | Every public header (section 2), unchanged, plus the generated `version.h`. |
134|| `lib/pkgconfig/qs.pc` | 0644 | From `qs.pc.in`, with `@PREFIX@` replaced by the `PREFIX` given to `make install` and `@VERSION@` by the version. |
135|| `share/man/man1/*.1` | 0644 | The manual page of each program. |
136|
137|Nothing else is installed. The prefix recorded in `qs.pc` is the one given to `make install`, also
138|when the build itself ran earlier with another or no `PREFIX`. A program that includes `qs/qs.h`
139|from the installed `include` directory and links the installed `libqs.a` with `-lm` must build
140|and behave like the programs in `build/bin`.
141|
142|## 9. Typical use
143|
144|    make -j8
145|    make -j8 check
146|    make install PREFIX=/usr DESTDIR=/tmp/stage
147|    make DEBUG=1

Read text file `/app/docs/colstat.md`.
1|# colstat
2|
3|    colstat [-d DELIM] [-c COLS] [--max-size N] [--version] [FILE]
4|
5|Reads a delimited text file from `FILE`, or from standard input when `FILE` is missing or `-`,
6|and prints summary statistics for its columns.
7|
8|## Options
9|
10|| Option | Meaning |
11||---|---|
12|| `-d DELIM` | Field delimiter: one character, or the word `tab`. Without `-d`: `,`. |
13|| `-c COLS` | Comma-separated column names, in the order to report them. A name may repeat. Without `-c`: every column in header order. |
14|| `--max-size N` | Refuse inputs larger than `N` bytes. `N` is a decimal number with an optional suffix: `k` or `K` (1024), `m` or `M` (1024 * 1024), `g` or `G` (1024 * 1024 * 1024). |
15|| `--version` | Print `colstat VERSION` and exit 0. |
16|
17|Options may appear in any order. An unknown option, a missing option value, a delimiter longer than
18|one character, or an invalid size is a usage error.
19|
20|## Input
21|
22|- Records end at `\n` or `\r\n`. Empty lines are ignored.
23|- The first record is the header and names the columns. Column names are compared exactly
24|  (case and blanks count). When a name occurs twice in the header, the first occurrence is used.
25|- A field that starts with `"` is quoted: it runs to the next `"` that is not doubled, `""`
26|  stands for one `"`, and delimiters and line breaks inside it are part of the field. Any text
27|  after the closing quote, up to the next delimiter, is appended to the field.
28|- A record with fewer fields than the header has empty values in the missing columns; extra
29|  fields are ignored.
30|- A value is numeric when, after removing spaces and tabs at both ends, it is an optional sign,
31|  digits with an optional decimal point (at least one digit before or after the point), and an
32|  optional exponent (`e` or `E`, optional sign, digits). Anything else (empty values, `NA`,
33|  `inf`, hexadecimal, decimal commas) is not counted.
34|
35|## Output
36|
37|One line per selected column, in the selected order:
38|
39|    NAME: count=N min=... max=... mean=... median=... p90=... stdev=...
40|
41|- `count` is the number of numeric values. When it is 0 the line ends after `count=0`.
42|- `mean` is the sum of the values in input order divided by the count.
43|- `median` is the middle value of the sorted values, or the mean of the two middle values.
44|- `p90` is the nearest-rank 90th percentile: the value at rank `ceil(0.9 * count)` in ascending order.
45|- `stdev` is the sample standard deviation (divisor `count - 1`), summed in input order; 0 when the
46|  count is below 2.
47|- Numbers are printed like C `printf("%.*g")` with `QS_STATS_PRECISION` significant digits
48|  (defined in `include/qs/stats.h`).
49|
50|## Exit status
51|
52|| Status | When |
53||---|---|
54|| 0 | Success. |
55|| 2 | Usage error, an empty input (no header), or a name in `-c` that is not a column. Nothing is printed on standard output. |
56|| 3 | The input is larger than `--max-size`. Nothing is printed on standard output. |
57|| 4 | The input cannot be read. |
58|
59|Error messages go to standard error.

Read text file `/app/docs/qcalc.md`.
1|# qcalc
2|
3|    qcalc [--version] [--ops] [-e EXPR] [FILE]
4|
5|Evaluates arithmetic expressions.
6|
7|- With `-e EXPR`, evaluates `EXPR` and prints one line.
8|- Otherwise reads `FILE` (or standard input when `FILE` is missing or `-`) and evaluates each line.
9|  A trailing `\r` is removed. Lines that are empty, contain only blanks, or whose first non-blank
10|  character is `#` are skipped. Every other line prints exactly one output line.
11|- `--version` prints `qcalc VERSION`; `--ops` prints the operation table the program was built with,
12|  one operation per line: `name token arity precedence assoc`, in the order of `src/ops.def`.
13|  Both exit 0 at once.
14|
15|## Grammar
16|
17|Tokens are numbers (digits with an optional decimal point and an optional exponent, or a decimal
18|point followed by digits), names (a letter or `_` followed by letters, digits or `_`, at most 31
19|characters), the symbols `+ - * / % ^`, parentheses and commas. Spaces and tabs separate tokens.
20|Any other character is an error.
21|
22|Expressions use the operations of `src/ops.def`:
23|
24|- Infix operators (`assoc` left or right, arity 2) bind by their precedence; a higher number binds
25|  tighter. Left-associative operators group from the left, right-associative ones from the right.
26|- A `-` where an operand is expected is the prefix operator `neg`. Its operand extends over every
27|  operator that binds tighter than `neg` itself, so the precedence in `src/ops.def` decides how a prefix `-` groups
28|  with the infix operators.
29|- Functions (`assoc` func) are called as `name(arg, ...)` with exactly `arity` arguments.
30|- Parentheses group as usual.
31|
32|## Results and errors
33|
34|A successful line prints the value like C `printf("%.10g")`. A failed line prints `error: ` and a
35|message; evaluation of that line stops at the first error. Messages:
36|
37|| Message | When |
38||---|---|
39|| `unexpected character 'C' at column N` | A character that starts no token. |
40|| `number out of range at column N` | A number too large for a double. |
41|| `name too long at column N` | A name of 32 or more characters. |
42|| `syntax error at column N` | A token that cannot appear where it is (N is its column, or one past the end of the line). |
43|| `unknown function 'NAME'` | A name that is not a function in the table. |
44|| `'NAME' takes N argument(s)` | A call with the wrong number of arguments (`argument` when N is 1). |
45|| `division by zero` | `/` or `%` with a zero right operand. |
46|| `domain error in 'TOKEN'` | An operation whose result is not a number (for example `sqrt` of a negative value). |
47|| `overflow in 'TOKEN'` | An operation whose result is infinite. |
48|
49|Columns count from 1. `%` is the C `fmod` remainder.
50|
51|## Exit status
52|
53|0 when every evaluated line succeeded, 1 when any line failed, 2 for usage errors, 4 when the input
54|cannot be read.

2|# Usage: genops.sh OPS_DEF > ops.h
3|# Writes the operation table header for the expression evaluator to stdout.

7|awk '
8|function fail(msg) { printf "%s:%d: %s\n", FILENAME, FNR, msg > "/dev/stderr"; bad = 1; exit 1 }
9|/^[ \t]*#/ || /^[ \t]*$/ { next }
10|{
11|    if (NF != 6) fail("expected 6 columns, found " NF)
12|    if ($3 !~ /^[0-9]+$/ || $4 !~ /^[0-9]+$/) fail("arity and precedence must be numbers")
13|    if ($5 == "left") a = "QS_LEFT"; else if ($5 == "right") a = "QS_RIGHT"; else if ($5 == "func") a = "QS_FUNC"; else fail("unknown assoc " $5)
14|    if ($1 in seen) fail("duplicate name " $1)
15|    seen[$1] = 1
16|    n++
17|    name[n] = $1; tok[n] = $2; arity[n] = $3; prec[n] = $4; assoc[n] = a; fn[n] = $6
18|}

20|    if (bad) exit 1

28|    print "enum qs_op_id {"
29|    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) printf "    QS_OP_%s,\n", toupper(name[i])
30|    print "};"
31|    print ""
32|    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) printf "double %s(const double *a);\n", fn[i]
33|    print ""

35|    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) printf "    { \"%s\", \"%s\", %d, %d, %s, %s }%s\n", name[i], tok[i], arity[i], prec[i], assoc[i], fn[i], (i < n ? ", \\" : "")

1|#!/bin/sh
2|# Usage: golden.sh BINDIR
3|# Runs every case in tests/golden against the programs in BINDIR. A case NAME has:
4|#   NAME.cmd     the program name and its arguments, one per line
5|#   NAME.in      standard input (optional; empty input when missing)
6|#   NAME.out     expected standard output
7|#   NAME.status  expected exit status (optional; 0 when missing)
8|# Prints one line per case and exits 1 when any case fails.
9|bindir=${1:?usage: golden.sh BINDIR}
10|dir=$(dirname "$0")/golden
11|cases=0
12|failed=0
13|for cmd in "$dir"/*.cmd; do
14|    [ -f "$cmd" ] || continue
15|    name=$(basename "$cmd" .cmd)
16|    cases=$((cases + 1))
17|    set --
18|    while IFS= read -r arg || [ -n "$arg" ]; do
19|        set -- "$@" "$arg"
20|    done < "$cmd"
21|    prog=$1
22|    shift
23|    input=/dev/null
24|    [ -f "$dir/$name.in" ] && input=$dir/$name.in
25|    want_status=0
26|    [ -f "$dir/$name.status" ] && want_status=$(cat "$dir/$name.status")
27|    got=$("$bindir/$prog" "$@" < "$input" 2>/dev/null)
28|    status=$?
29|    want=$(cat "$dir/$name.out")
30|    if [ "$status" -eq "$want_status" ] && [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then
31|        echo "PASS $name"
32|    else
33|        echo "FAIL $name (exit $status, expected $want_status)"
34|        failed=$((failed + 1))
35|    fi
36|done
37|echo "golden: $cases cases, $failed failed"
38|[ "$failed" -eq 0 ]

# Durable Test Collateral

Verification is part of the delivered project when it can prevent the same
behavior from breaking again. Use the project's existing framework and
conventions.

Loading this skill does not mean the current turn asked for the change. While you
are still investigating — explaining existing behavior, or answering a design
question the user raised — use commands that only read and leave the repository
unmodified, tests included.

## Scale to the task

Skip the failing-test-first workflow below when the change is tiny and leaves
program logic alone (a typo, a text or style tweak, a config value, or a version
pin), when the work is a throwaway prototype or a standalone one-file script or
page, when the request adds features to a project you created earlier in this
session, or when the user asks for speed or a quick result. A quick direct check
of the changed behavior is enough there; if you add no maintained test, say so in
the report. A user request for tests anywhere in the session, or a
specification that makes tests a deliverable, still applies.

Any other bug fix or behavior change keeps the workflow at its smallest: one
focused failing test, the fix, that test passing, and, when a broad run is
required, one broad run after the final edit. A report that something already
built behaves wrongly is a bug fix, even when it comes with feature requests.

Before a test run that may take more than a minute or two, tell the user in one
line what runs and why. If you poll it, post a short status line between polls;
never poll a long run silently.

## Keep the check with the project

For a bug fix or behavior change, add or update the smallest maintained test in
the repository's normal test layout that exercises the changed behavior. If a
specification makes a reusable suite or test category a deliverable, implement
that suite instead of treating it as private verification.

An inline interpreter command, heredoc, scratch script, temporary-directory
test, demo, or manual probe may help diagnose the problem, but it does not
replace the maintained test. Keep a useful self-authored test unless the user
explicitly asks for a disposable probe.

Do not add a new test framework solely to satisfy this skill. If the repository
has no maintained harness and the request does not require one, disclose when
durable coverage would be disproportionate or infeasible and use the narrowest
honest verification instead.

On a later turn, update the maintained test even when the old suite remains
green and the user does not repeat the test request. Cover the new behavior,
not merely an unrelated cleanup in the test file.

## Prove the maintained check

Observe the authentic failure before the implementation change when it is safe
and runnable. Then make the smallest implementation change and run the focused
maintained test after the final relevant source or test edit.

Do not weaken or delete a real failing test to obtain green. Fix the product,
or explain why the test's expectation is wrong before changing that
expectation. Do not repeat an unchanged check solely to collect evidence.

Run a broad or full suite only when the user, a repository gate, or
proportionate risk requires it, and then once, after the final edit, rather
than after each intermediate edit. A focused regression test comes first; broad
proof does not substitute for missing focused coverage.

Before deciding what a repository gate requires, read what the repository
declares it runs: its CI workflow, its test entry points, and its root-level
scripts listed with hidden entries included. A suite the project itself runs
over this change is a gate, not an optional extra, and a suite that skips
itself when its data is absent is not a green result.

A runner is unavailable only after you tried to make it available. When the
repository ships the command that fetches or builds the missing fixture,
corpus, or toolchain, run that command once and then run the gate. Report the
gate unavailable only when that attempt itself failed, and say what failed.

If the real runner is unavailable but the focused test can still be authored
honestly, leave the focused test in the repository and say it was not run. Do
not fabricate a passing result.

1|# colstat
2|
3|    colstat [-d DELIM] [-c COLS] [--max-size N] [--version] [FILE]
4|
5|Reads a delimited text file from `FILE`, or from standard input when `FILE` is missing or `-`,
6|and prints summary statistics for its columns.
7|
8|## Options
9|
10|| Option | Meaning |
11||---|---|
12|| `-d DELIM` | Field delimiter: one character, or the word `tab`. Without `-d`: `,`. |
13|| `-c COLS` | Comma-separated column names, in the order to report them. A name may repeat. Without `-c`: every column in header order. |
14|| `--max-size N` | Refuse inputs larger than `N` bytes. `N` is a decimal number with an optional suffix: `k` or `K` (1024), `m` or `M` (1024 * 1024), `g` or `G` (1024 * 1024 * 1024). |
15|| `--version` | Print `colstat VERSION` and exit 0. |
16|
17|Options may appear in any order. An unknown option, a missing option value, a delimiter longer than
18|one character, or an invalid size is a usage error.
19|
20|## Input
21|
22|- Records end at `\n` or `\r\n`. Empty lines are ignored.
23|- The first record is the header and names the columns. Column names are compared exactly
24|  (case and blanks count). When a name occurs twice in the header, the first occurrence is used.
25|- A field that starts with `"` is quoted: it runs to the next `"` that is not doubled, `""`
26|  stands for one `"`, and delimiters and line breaks inside it are part of the field. Any text
27|  after the closing quote, up to the next delimiter, is appended to the field.
28|- A record with fewer fields than the header has empty values in the missing columns; extra
29|  fields are ignored.
30|- A value is numeric when, after removing spaces and tabs at both ends, it is an optional sign,
31|  digits with an optional decimal point (at least one digit before or after the point), and an
32|  optional exponent (`e` or `E`, optional sign, digits). Anything else (empty values, `NA`,
33|  `inf`, hexadecimal, decimal commas) is not counted.
34|
35|## Output
36|
37|One line per selected column, in the selected order:
38|
39|    NAME: count=N min=... max=... mean=... median=... p90=... stdev=...
40|
41|- `count` is the number of numeric values. When it is 0 the line ends after `count=0`.
42|- `mean` is the sum of the values in input order divided by the count.
43|- `median` is the middle value of the sorted values, or the mean of the two middle values.
44|- `p90` is the nearest-rank 90th percentile: the value at rank `ceil(0.9 * count)` in ascending order.
45|- `stdev` is the sample standard deviation (divisor `count - 1`), summed in input order; 0 when the
46|  count is below 2.
47|- Numbers are printed like C `printf("%.*g")` with `QS_STATS_PRECISION` significant digits
48|  (defined in `include/qs/stats.h`).
49|
50|## Exit status
51|
52|| Status | When |
53||---|---|
54|| 0 | Success. |
55|| 2 | Usage error, an empty input (no header), or a name in `-c` that is not a column. Nothing is printed on standard output. |
56|| 3 | The input is larger than `--max-size`. Nothing is printed on standard output. |
57|| 4 | The input cannot be read. |
58|
59|Error messages go to standard error.</tool-result>

1|# qcalc
2|
3|    qcalc [--version] [--ops] [-e EXPR] [FILE]
4|
5|Evaluates arithmetic expressions.
6|
7|- With `-e EXPR`, evaluates `EXPR` and prints one line.
8|- Otherwise reads `FILE` (or standard input when `FILE` is missing or `-`) and evaluates each line.
9|  A trailing `\r` is removed. Lines that are empty, contain only blanks, or whose first non-blank
10|  character is `#` are skipped. Every other line prints exactly one output line.
11|- `--version` prints `qcalc VERSION`; `--ops` prints the operation table the program was built with,
12|  one operation per line: `name token arity precedence assoc`, in the order of `src/ops.def`.
13|  Both exit 0 at once.
14|
15|## Grammar
16|
17|Tokens are numbers (digits with an optional decimal point and an optional exponent, or a decimal
18|point followed by digits), names (a letter or `_` followed by letters, digits or `_`, at most 31
19|characters), the symbols `+ - * / % ^`, parentheses and commas. Spaces and tabs separate tokens.
20|Any other character is an error.
21|
22|Expressions use the operations of `src/ops.def`:
23|
24|- Infix operators (`assoc` left or right, arity 2) bind by their precedence; a higher number binds
25|  tighter. Left-associative operators group from the left, right-associative ones from the right.
26|- A `-` where an operand is expected is the prefix operator `neg`. Its operand extends over every
27|  operator that binds tighter than `neg` itself, so the precedence in `src/ops.def` decides how a prefix `-` groups
28|  with the infix operators.
29|- Functions (`assoc` func) are called as `name(arg, ...)` with exactly `arity` arguments.
30|- Parentheses group as usual.
31|
32|## Results and errors
33|
34|A successful line prints the value like C `printf("%.10g")`. A failed line prints `error: ` and a
35|message; evaluation of that line stops at the first error. Messages:
36|
37|| Message | When |
38||---|---|
39|| `unexpected character 'C' at column N` | A character that starts no token. |
40|| `number out of range at column N` | A number too large for a double. |
41|| `name too long at column N` | A name of 32 or more characters. |
42|| `syntax error at column N` | A token that cannot appear where it is (N is its column, or one past the end of the line). |
43|| `unknown function 'NAME'` | A name that is not a function in the table. |
44|| `'NAME' takes N argument(s)` | A call with the wrong number of arguments (`argument` when N is 1). |
45|| `division by zero` | `/` or `%` with a zero right operand. |
46|| `domain error in 'TOKEN'` | An operation whose result is not a number (for example `sqrt` of a negative value). |
47|| `overflow in 'TOKEN'` | An operation whose result is infinite. |
48|
49|Columns count from 1. `%` is the C `fmod` remainder.
50|
51|## Exit status
52|
53|0 when every evaluated line succeeded, 1 when any line failed, 2 for usage errors, 4 when the input
54|cannot be read.</tool-result>
